A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work, renamed from MARS to MARSHAL. The methods, equations, figures, tables, prompts, and retained appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original game-playing experiments, downstream reasoning evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds model-scaling experiments, controlled comparisons, and supplementary analyses in Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The self-play procedure, turn-level cumulative-return estimator, agent-specific centering, objectives, rewards, and prompts remain unchanged. MARSHAL is a renaming; the 8B experiment and alternative algorithms are experimental configurations and controls.

E1.justification: Both retain training on Tic-Tac-Toe, Kuhn Poker, and Mini Hanabi; testing on Connect Four, Leduc Hold’em, and Simple Hanabi; and the same seven reasoning benchmarks under single-agent, MAD, and AutoGen settings. The added experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds direct MT-GRPO comparisons on games and downstream MAD/AutoGen tasks (Tables 10–11). Tables 7–9 also introduce explicit SPIRAL RAE trained on the full game portfolio and competitive-only MARSHAL controls, substantially expanding comparisons relevant to the algorithm’s contribution.

E3.justification: Appendices D–G introduce Qwen3-8B training and evaluation, controlled algorithm-versus-game-curriculum experiments, and penalty-weight settings of 0, 0.5, and 1. New analyses measure failure categories, response length, and overlong-response losses. These substantially expand the experimental design without establishing reruns of the retained 4B experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative GPQA failure analysis (Figure 5), player-role return distributions (Figure 6), algorithm/curriculum disentanglement (Appendix E), and length-penalty sensitivity and failure analysis (Appendix G). These address mechanisms and robustness questions beyond v1’s retained qualitative examples and component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 1000-game evaluation count is retained. New return distributions and failure percentages are descriptive analyses, without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for 8B models, comparison methods, failure categories, and penalty sensitivity. For example, its new Table 6 reports MAD averages of 82.49 for Qwen3-8B and 85.09 for MARSHAL-8B. Original Table 1 and raw appendix results remain unchanged, while Tables 3–4 replace normalized poker values: the Tic-Tac-Toe specialist’s Kuhn scores change from 42.90/-77.80 to 74.15/3.42 despite unchanged raw returns.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, four numbered equations, and GAE equivalence argument are retained. Appendix F.1 adds conceptual explanations of MT-GRPO’s limitations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central methodological and transfer claims remain. The abstract and introduction reduce the claimed GPQA gain from 12.5% to 6.6% and add a 3.5% average-gain claim. The revised GPQA claim still conflicts with unchanged Table 1: MAD scores of 37.88 and 45.45 imply 7.57 percentage points, rather than Section 4.3’s 6.57.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking transfer to peer-input use and task focus, cooperative curricula to AutoGen performance, MT-GRPO weaknesses to variable-length normalization, and length penalties to avoiding overlong failures. It also expands N-player limitations. Some interpretation remains problematic: Section 4.4’s approximately 7% reduction in System Design Issues conflicts with Figure 5’s labels of 29.5 and 13.9.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page and model-collection access links, VS-Bench implementation attribution, normalization reference points, and explanations of the length bounds. However, Appendix C removes v1’s downstream decoding settings: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The core hyperparameter table and prompt listings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that SPIRAL’s role-conditioned estimator is analogous to its agent-specific normalization and develops a substantial comparison with MT-GRPO in Section 5 and Appendix F. This materially refines positioning of the central contributions. Additional citations cover the failure taxonomy, VS-Bench, automated workflows, and a self-play survey.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, competitive/cooperative terminology is standardized, and explanatory prose is edited throughout. Section 4.4 gains an expanded heading, and new appendix sections precede the retained material. The main narrative structure and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are redrawn with revised styling, labels, and legends; Figures 5–6 and eight experimental tables are added. Main and appendix tables are regrouped and reformatted, including replacing green/red highlighting with bold, underlining, and row shading. These constitute a substantial visual revision.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical attribution through matched algorithm comparisons and separate curriculum controls in Appendices E–F, addressing an important gap in v1. The 8B experiments and penalty analysis further test scalability and robustness, while revised related work clarifies methodological overlap. These gains outweigh the remaining GPQA arithmetic discrepancy, the new Figure 5 labeling inconsistency, and the loss of evaluation decoding details.
